policies.title: Maldives and Nepal ordinary passports: visa-free entry
policies.summary: DGIP's current visa-abolition schedule identifies Maldives and Nepal as the only two all-national ordinary-passport visitor exemptions.
conditions: The current DGIP schedule gives Maldives nationals three months and Nepal nationals one month without a visa; an extension is required after the stated period.

This records ordinary visitor passports only. It does not establish work, residence, overseas-Pakistani origin, diplomatic/official/special document, transit, security, or individual-admissibility treatment.

policies.title: Qatar ordinary passports: direct visa on arrival
policies.summary: DGIP grants all Qatari passport holders, including ordinary passports, visa on arrival without the ETA requirement that applies to the other listed tourist-VOA nationalities.
conditions: The current DGIP page says the route is available at any port of entry, free of charge, for 30 days and extendable another 30 days, with single or multiple entries.
Requires a passport valid for at least six months, a confirmed return ticket, and cash equivalent to USD 1,500 or a valid credit card.
It does not establish work, residence, Indian-origin religious tourism, group-tour, diplomatic/official/special-document, security or individual-admissibility treatment.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: tourist Visa Prior to Arrival / ETA
policies.summary: For these named tourist nationalities, Pakistan labels the visa as visa on arrival but requires electronic travel authorization 48-72 hours before travel. This candidate normalizes that required advance authorization as ETA rather than a true walk-up VOA.
conditions: The DGIP list names 50 tourist-VOA nationalities; Nepal and Maldives use the easier visa-free route and Qatar has the direct no-ETA VOA route recorded separately.
Submit the ETA/VPA intent 48-72 hours before travel. The arrival-issued tourist visa is up to three months under the category page.
A 2025 MFA release says the mobile-app VPA category serves eligible nationals of 120 countries but does not name them. It cannot safely expand or replace DGIP's named 50-country table.

Requires the category's passport, photograph, and sponsor invitation or hotel-booking evidence. It does not establish business-only VOA, Indian-origin religious tourism, designated-tour-operator groups, residence, work, special documents, security or individual admission.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: tourist eVisa
policies.summary: DGIP's live 175-country eVisa schedule establishes the online tourist-visa route for these passports; easier visa-free, named VPA/ETA, and direct-VOA routes above take precedence.
conditions: The official page says applicants from 175 countries can apply for eVisa and that the route is augmented with ETA; use the official online visa system before travel.
The newer MFA mobile-app release reports an unnamed 120-country VPA cohort. Because it supplies no country list, it does not safely prove an easier VPA route for any particular eVisa-only passport.

For tourist/visit travel, DGIP requires the ordinary passport, photograph, and a sponsor invitation or hotel booking. The listed standard tourist visa is up to three months with double entry and can be extended subject to the stated limits.

The policy does not establish business-only routes, overseas-Pakistani origin or family arrangements, work, residence, transit, group tourism, diplomatic/official/special documents, prohibited areas, security or individual-admissibility rights.

policies.title: List-A-only ordinary passports: advance tourist visa
policies.summary: Pakistan's current List-A schedule authorizes missions to grant these ordinary-passport holders a standard tourist visa, while they are not in the current 175-country eVisa schedule or a more favorable ordinary visitor route.
conditions: DGIP authorizes missions to grant List-A foreigners a visit/tourist visa with three months' validity and stay and double entry; use the online visa process as directed by MFA.

This policy records the ordinary tourist advance-visa baseline only. It does not establish a business, work, residence, transit, group-tour, diplomatic/official/special-document, security or individual-admissibility outcome.
